rationale.conceptual: The DFT method itself is well-established, but reproducing the paper's specific protocol involves several non-trivial components: constructing a 3×3 s-triazine g-C3N4 supercell with a 15 Å vacuum layer, selecting appropriate pseudopotentials, applying Grimme D2 dispersion, optimizing multiple adsorption configurations, and implementing external electric fields. These steps demand solid understanding beyond routine textbook exercises, yet do not involve novel algorithm design.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans three stages with numerous interdependent calculations: 18 pristine adsorption optimizations, 3 doped slab relaxations, ~54 doped adsorption optimizations, and 27 field-perturbed optimizations. Orchestrating this many DFT runs (Quantum ESPRESSO), managing I/O, extracting precise numeric values (adsorption energies, charge transfers, geometries), and assembling them into strict JSON schemas is a fragile, multi-tool engineering task.

difficulty.reasoning: The task demands multiple DFT geometry optimizations across pristine and doped surfaces under varying electric fields. While the underlying method (PBE-D2) is standard, the correct setup of the supercell, dispersion correction, and field application requires careful domain knowledge, and orchestrating ~100 separate simulations into structured JSON outputs is a substantial engineering challenge.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All DFT calculations use a modest 3×3 supercell, 290 eV cutoff, and 3×3×1 k-points, making them CPU-only. Each run consumes roughly 4 GB RAM; input structures and output files are tiny, totaling well under 0.1 GB.
